findings.claim: Neither published request_hash is the hash of an action: event 1 is exactly SHA-256 of the empty string and event 2 is a rearrangement of the same bytes, so the audit record does not say what was evaluated
findings.severity: the chain still verifies, so this is a weakness in the example rather than a break in the scheme

findings.claim: NTI-1's reference implementation ube-foundation is PolyForm Shield, not an open licence, so it cannot be vendored into an Apache-2.0 harness
findings.observed: PolyForm Shield 1.0.0 named in the project description badge

findings.claim: The AlgoVoi Keystone fully answers 3 of 7 NTI-1 requirements, partly 2, and not at all 2
findings.method: derived from src/algovoi_ube/keystone_mapping.py, itself written against docs.algovoi.co.uk/keystone and the NTI-1 text

pillars.nti_requirement: Principal-bound identity; actions signed by a key delegated by the principal
pillars.note: The Agent Passport is the identity tier of the keystone chain, and the passport_ref is a load-bearing field of every downstream reference, so identity is bound into the decision rather than attached to it.

pillars.nti_requirement: Every action evaluated against policy; capability caveats Expires, MaxExecutions, ValueLimit, PathRestricted; deny must not execute
pillars.note: The mandate is authority and the policy binding fixes the policy in force. Because policy_bound_ref is hashed into decision_ref, an action cannot be authorised under one policy and executed under another.

pillars.nti_requirement: BFT consensus for high-value multi-agent actions; threshold signature collection over (voter_id, request_id, decision, outcome_hash, signature)
pillars.note: Keystone composes one chain per action and does not define a voting or threshold protocol. This is the one pillar it does not answer.
pillars.gap: Needs a threshold signature layer above the keystone: collect votes over the decision_ref, then require the threshold before the execution tier is reached.

pillars.nti_requirement: Tamper-evident audit trail, SHA-256 chained, every evaluated action recorded with decision and reason
pillars.note: decision_ref records what was authorised and execution_ref records what actually happened and binds back to that decision. A verifier can confirm the executed action is consistent with the decision rather than merely correlated with it.

pillars.nti_requirement: State and audit trail persist across restarts with self-verifying integrity; exportable and importable
pillars.note: The chain is content-addressed, so reloading it re-verifies every link by recomputation with no issuer contact. Keystone does not itself define a persistence store or an export format.
pillars.gap: Needs a store of record and an export envelope; the chain verifies independently once landed.

pillars.nti_requirement: Fail-closed on unreachable or non-authoritative registry; incomplete_check with reason tryLater, not_authoritative or internal_error
pillars.note: Keystone provides the *evidence* that authority lapsed, because the mandate and revocation state carry their own references and validity windows. It does not define the runtime halt behaviour.
pillars.gap: The halt is a runtime decision, which this repo implements. The clean split is: Keystone proves the state, the sidecar acts on it.

pillars.nti_requirement: Interoperability with the ASL Conformance Kit over AF_UNIX sockets
pillars.note: Keystone is transport-agnostic and says nothing about sandboxing.
pillars.gap: Unchanged by any keystone decision; this is an adapter concern.

flow.keystone_call: passport_ref from the Agent Passport tier
mandate_ref from the Payment Mandate tier
policy_bound_ref from the Policy Binding tier
not in Keystone; a threshold signing layer over decision_ref

findings.claim: An incomplete_check receipt cannot be constructed with an unclassified reason, so a failure cannot masquerade as a pass

The REVERIFY to RESUMED edge is a declared transition that can be withdrawn without inventing a terminal state, it cannot be walked directly without a recorded basis, and an irreversible-revocation refusal leaves the chain where it started, so irreversibility lives in the missing edge rather than in a stuck label
findings.method: inspect the transition table, attempt a resume under an irreversible revocation and confirm the chain stays in PAUSE, then walk the declared edge directly and confirm it is refused

findings.claim: A valid signature alone does not reach RESUMED; a resume has to carry a complete basis from a closed set, so a restored condition and an accepted risk cannot produce identical records, and an evidence basis with no evidence attached is refused rather than read as a signature-only resume
findings.method: decide_resume with no basis, with an evidence basis carrying no evidence object, with a complete evidence basis, and with a basis reporting a revoked delegation

empty_evidence_basis.error: an evidence based resume needs at least one restore condition, a verifier role and a validity window; a signature alone is an authenticity check, not a restore condition check

lifecycle_no_basis.error: resume refused: a resume must carry a basis (evidence or exemption); reaching RESUMED on no basis records nothing about why the halt was lifted

empty_exemption_basis.error: an exemption basis must record why the risk was accepted and who accepted it; an exemption with no reason and no accountable actor is an accepted risk that nobody owns

findings.claim: An exemption covers a policy violation and cannot cover a revocation or an undetermined authority, so a signed exemption cannot buy back the fail closed property

attempts.refused_because: exemption does not cover authority_revoked. Revocation is the issuing authority's decision; a manager on the executing side cannot un-revoke someone else's authority.
exemption does not cover authority_not_determined. An absence of information is not a judgement about it; a signature cannot convert 'we do not know' into 'we know'.

findings.claim: The wire value does not depend on the receipt being present, so a PAUSE with no receipt is still a well formed record and the wire value set stays closed
A policy violation is denied under STRICT and paused under VOC, and a revocation halts under VOC rather than becoming an exemption candidate

A receipt that purports to exempt a revocation or an undetermined authority cannot be expressed: the schema admits only policy_violation, the constructor refuses the others, and the grader will not sign them
A receipt whose justification is edited after signing does not resume the halted action, so the signature is load bearing rather than decorative

tampered_receipt.reason: the receipt signature did not verify, so the pause stands

findings.claim: The canonicaliser follows RFC 8785 where it differs from Python's json: ECMAScript number layout, UTF-16 key ordering, and literal non-ASCII rather than \uXXXX escaping
Signatures use CRYSTALS-Dilithium5 as ML-DSA-87 in an isolated process, so the key never enters the Python process that assembles the receipt
findings.method: sign a real payload in the Rust core, verify it, tamper with it, and attempt an empty payload

findings.claim: A capability proof built against a superseded registry root is refused at the boundary, while the same proof still verifies against the historical root for audit
findings.method: prove membership, revoke, then verify against the current and the pinned root
findings.stale_reason: the proof was built for root 2cc1ed7d5e2a but 39a37abed378 is the root in force, so it is stale

findings.claim: The declared boundary lets the atomic call in flight finish and refuses the next one, which is the posture NTI requires, and the effect boundary that would interrupt mid call is identifiable as non-compliant

An automated grader cannot accept risk on its own authority: it cannot issue its own mandate, it signs nothing without one, and the mandate's policy scope, principal scope, value ceiling, expiry and revocation are all enforced at the moment of signing
